question: Is the parallel-run protocol's uniqueness clause (<= 70% of emitted dots within 3 px of any earlier raster) jointly satisfiable with the same protocol's clause 1 (a dense, image-like field)? For which added mass M does the emitted union clear the like-for-like reading, and which comparators are non-decidable?

provenance.method: ad-hoc invocation of scripts/build_h71_field.py (build_field + greedy_order), then 3-px overlap measured against the named comparators with scipy.ndimage.distance_transform_edt (literal reading: fraction of emitted dots inside the distance-3 neighbourhood of the comparator) and a greedy one-to-one cKDTree matching (matched reading: each comparator dot absorbs at most one emitted dot).
provenance.runner: not the H80 runner; the numbers are clause diagnostics and carry no DTI/G2 reading
provenance.reproduce: build the restricted field (BH.build_field(grid, 'restricted')), take the top M of BH.greedy_order(score, allowed, 200000, 2.8), union with the champion mask, measure.

restricted_pool.note: the pool, not the ladder, is the binding constraint on M: 91,370 dots are available under 2.8-px non-maximum suppression

champion_reference.note: the already-scored champion itself is 99.9% inside the 3-px neighbourhood of the dense lattice comparator

reading.like_for_like_clause: against the one discriminating dot-field comparator (gems60-h72-union, itself a GEMS-60-family artifact), the 70% limit is crossed between M = 24,000 (0.7167) and M = 30,000 (0.6535), i.e. at a union of about 62,000-68,000 dots - five to six times the 12,000-dot mass the H80 eligibility ladder selected. The emitted M = 12,000 artifact is 0.8864 and fails.
reading.universal_blockers: calib_r13lattice_00904, r13_lattice_s5_00904, r11_greedy_mp and r14_union_tips10_lat6 are within 3 px of >= 70% of the footprint themselves (measured footprint fractions 0.9987 / 0.9987 / 0.7397 / 0.7620). For any emission covering most of the footprint the clause's own limit is already exceeded by the comparator, so the clause carries no discriminating information against them; a mass-matched random emission scores 0.9987 literal / 0.8746 matched against the lattice and 0.7011 / 0.6401 against r11, while the H72-union comparator gives a random emission 0.0402 / 0.0343.

conclusion: Clause 1 (dense field) and clause 3 read literally (including the lattice comparators) are jointly unsatisfiable: the champion alone is 0.99915 inside the lattice, so ANY emission containing the champion fails, and omitting the champion discards the only live-scored mass. Read like-for-like (the clause's own 70% limit applied to comparators that are themselves below it), clause 3 needs a union of at least about 64,000 dots - the emitted 49,654-dot restricted union fails at 0.8864. Because the G2 holdout reading deteriorates with this added mass (H80: -0.000541 at 12,000 versus H72's -0.000288 at 6,000), a like-for-like-compliant larger emission is not a path to a better score; it is a protocol experiment and would be experiment 4, outside the 3-experiment budget.
